newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt says 97/98 budget ideas preliminary.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt says 97/98 budget ideas preliminary.

text.p: The South African government on Monday declined to confirm or deny weekend reports that the cabinet had accepted a tough spending budget for 1997/98.

A finance department spokeswoman reiterated that the government remained committed cutting the budget deficit to four percent of GDP in 1997/98 from 5.1 percent this year, but said any numbers at this stage were preliminary.
"At this stage all figures are soft," she said.
The Sunday Times reported that government had backed a 185.5 billion rand budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year, starting next April.
That compares with this year's budget of 173.659 billion rand, and in real terms would represent a spending cut of over two percent, assuming annual inflation of nine percent.
The Sunday Times quoted documents in its possession showing that the 185.5 billion rand figure was approved at a cabinet meeting last month.

According to the documents, the expenditure figure includes a contingency reserve of one billion rand and an unallocated reserve of 2.4 billion. These amounts would be used to finance national disasters and "unmanageable" expenditure in the provinces respectively.
